indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.5.1.1 Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Identify the causes and effects of foul body odour on humans and how it can be prevented

skills.description: Identify causes of foul body odour (e.g. poor bathing habits, dirty clothes, sweat, certain foods).
State effects of body odour on humans (e.g. social embarrassment, low confidence, rejection).
Identify ways to prevent body odour (e.g. bathing regularly, using deodorant, wearing clean clothes, using lime/lemon).
Describe daily hygiene habits that prevent body odour.
Identify materials used to prevent body odour (e.g. soap, deodorant, lime, lemon).
Plan a simple project on eliminating foul body odour.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Body odour is caused by eating too much.
Deodorant is the only way to prevent body odour.
Body odour is not a health issue.
Bathing once a week prevents body odour.
Lime and lemon have no use in hygiene.
Dirty clothes do not cause body odour.

questions.stem: Which of these can cause foul body odour?
hints: Think about what happens when sweat stays on the body.
questions.explanation: Not bathing regularly allows sweat and dirt to collect on the body, causing foul body odour.
questions.misconception: Body odour is caused by eating too much.

questions.stem: Ama wears the same uniform for one week without washing it. What is likely to happen?
options: The uniform will smell and may cause body odour
hints: Sweat and dirt collect on worn clothes.
questions.explanation: Wearing unwashed clothes allows sweat and dirt to collect, causing body odour.
questions.misconception: Dirty clothes do not cause body odour.

questions.stem: Give one cause of foul body odour.
questions.explanation: Causes of body odour include poor bathing habits, dirty clothes and sweat.
questions.misconception: Body odour is caused by eating too much.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a cause of body odour?
hints: Which action keeps the body clean?
questions.explanation: Bathing regularly prevents body odour; it does not cause it. Dirty clothes, sweat and poor hygiene can cause body odour.
questions.misconception: Bathing causes body odour.

questions.stem: How can foul body odour affect a person?
options: It can make them feel embarrassed
hints: Think about how people react to bad smell.
questions.explanation: Foul body odour can make a person feel embarrassed and less confident.
questions.misconception: Body odour is not a health issue.

questions.stem: State one effect of body odour on a person.
questions.explanation: Body odour can cause embarrassment, low confidence and social rejection.
questions.misconception: Body odour has no effect.

questions.stem: Why might a learner with body odour be avoided by classmates?
questions.explanation: A learner with body odour may be avoided because the smell is unpleasant, which can affect their social relationships.
questions.misconception: Body odour is not a problem.

questions.stem: Which of these helps prevent body odour?
questions.explanation: Bathing regularly helps prevent body odour by removing sweat and dirt.
questions.misconception: Bathing once a week prevents body odour.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way to prevent body odour?
options: Wearing the same clothes for a week
Not drying the body after bathing
questions.explanation: Using deodorant after bathing helps prevent body odour.
questions.misconception: Deodorant is the only way to prevent body odour.

questions.stem: Give one way to prevent body odour.
questions.explanation: Ways to prevent body odour include bathing regularly, wearing clean clothes, using deodorant and using lime or lemon.
questions.misconception: Body odour cannot be prevented.

questions.stem: A pupil uses lime or lemon on the armpit after bathing. Why is this useful?
hints: Lime and lemon have a strong smell.
They can help control body odour.
questions.explanation: Lime or lemon can help reduce body odour because of their strong, fresh smell.
questions.misconception: Lime and lemon have no use in hygiene.

questions.stem: Which daily habit helps prevent body odour?
options: Bathing at least twice a day
questions.explanation: Bathing at least twice a day helps prevent body odour by keeping the body clean.
questions.misconception: Bathing once a week is enough.

questions.stem: Describe one daily hygiene habit that prevents body odour.
hints: Think about what you do every day.
questions.explanation: A daily hygiene habit that prevents body odour is bathing regularly with soap and water.
questions.misconception: Hygiene habits do not affect body odour.

questions.stem: Which set lists good daily habits to prevent body odour?
options: Bathe twice daily, wear clean clothes, use deodorant
Bathe once a week, wear dirty clothes, avoid soap
Bathe once a month, wear the same clothes, avoid water
Never bathe, wear dirty socks, use no soap
hints: Good habits keep the body clean.
questions.explanation: Good daily habits include bathing twice daily, wearing clean clothes and using deodorant.
questions.misconception: Bathing once a week is enough.

questions.stem: Which materials are used to prevent body odour?
hints: Think about what you use in the bathroom.
questions.explanation: Soap and deodorant are used to prevent body odour.
questions.misconception: Deodorant is the only material used.

questions.stem: Name two materials used to prevent body odour.
questions.explanation: Materials used to prevent body odour include soap, water, deodorant, lime and lemon.
questions.misconception: Lime and lemon have no use.

questions.stem: Why is soap important in preventing body odour?
options: It removes sweat and dirt from the body
It makes the body smell stronger
questions.explanation: Soap is important because it removes sweat and dirt from the body, helping prevent body odour.
questions.misconception: Soap causes body odour.

questions.stem: Plan a simple project to help your class reduce body odour. Write three steps you will take (e.g. make a poster, organise a hygiene talk, create a reminder chart).

criteria.description: Wrote three clear steps for the project
Steps are relevant to reducing body odour
Plan is realistic for a class project

hints: Think about what you can do in class.
Posters and talks are good ideas.
questions.explanation: This is a written task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Body odour cannot be addressed in a project.

questions.stem: Design a poster for your school to teach learners how to prevent body odour. Show at least two actions, such as bathing and using deodorant.

criteria.description: Showed at least two correct actions to prevent body odour
Used clear drawings or symbols for each action
Included short words or labels to explain the actions
Poster is clear and suitable for learners

hints: Think about bathing and clean clothes.
Use drawings of soap, water, and deodorant.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Body odour is not a health issue.

questions.stem: Why is it important to plan a project on body odour?
answer: to help people learn how to prevent it
to raise awareness and improve hygiene
to teach others about good hygiene
questions.explanation: Planning a project on body odour is important to raise awareness and teach people how to prevent it.
questions.misconception: Projects on body odour are not useful.
